title: Trading in Company Securities Policy

tiers.name: Genesis Energy Persons
tiers.description: All Genesis Energy Directors, officers, employees, contractors and secondees at Genesis Energy, including its subsidiaries (the Genesis Energy Group).

tiers.name: Restricted Persons
tiers.description: All Directors of members of the Genesis Energy Group; the Chief Executive and all senior managers reporting to the Chief Executive and those directly reporting to those persons; trusts and companies controlled by such persons; and anyone else notified by the General Counsel and Company Secretary as subject to these additional restrictions.

tiers.name: Directors and Chief Executive (other than the Chairman of the Board)
tiers.description: Sub-group of Restricted Persons distinguished only for clearance: consent requests are presented to the Chairman of the Board.

tiers.name: Chairman of the Board
tiers.description: Sub-group of Restricted Persons distinguished only for clearance: the Chairman's own consent requests are presented to the Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee (or, for a Blackout Period request in that person's absence, the Chairman of the Human Resources and Remuneration Committee).

tiers.name: Restricted Persons (other than Directors and the Chief Executive)
tiers.description: Sub-group of Restricted Persons distinguished only for clearance: consent requests are presented to the Chief Executive.

tiers.name: Spouse and dependant of a Restricted Person
tiers.description: The Restricted Person must ensure the same pre-approval and information requirements are complied with, including completing the Request for Consent to Trade form, on behalf of their spouse or dependant.

definitions.hedging_definition: An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Genesis Energy Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.

windows.end_anchor: first trading day after the full-year results are released to NZX and ASX
first trading day after the half-year results are released to NZX and ASX

windows.start_anchor: 30 days prior to release of a prospectus for a general public offer of the same class of Securities

ad_hoc_blackout_authority: The General Counsel and Company Secretary may specify any other Blackout Period from time to time. The Policy does not address whether such an ad hoc Blackout Period, or a refusal of consent, must be kept confidential.

rules.detail: Securities is expressly defined to include options and derivatives (including futures) created over or in respect of Genesis Energy Group securities, so an OTC put/call is Trading. Ordinary Genesis Energy Persons face no pre-approval requirement, only the insider trading and short-term trading rules.
rules.evidence: Any other securities of Genesis Energy or any member of the Genesis Energy Group and any options or derivatives (including futures contracts quoted on an authorised futures exchange) created over or in respect of any securities of any member of the Genesis Energy Group

rules.detail: Restricted Persons must obtain written pre-approval for any Trading in Securities, which by definition includes options and derivatives created over Genesis Energy securities.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.

rules.detail: Ban on entering any transaction for an 'Associated Product' that limits the economic risk of an entitlement under an equity-based remuneration scheme, applying to all Genesis Energy Persons while the entitlement remains unvested.
rules.evidence: Where Genesis Energy Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'.

rules.detail: The Associated Product ban is framed around a person's 'entitlement' under a remuneration scheme, not securities already vested and held; once vested, hedging is caught only as ordinary Trading, subject to insider trading and short-term rules but no pre-approval for non-Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: 'Trading' in Securities means buying or selling securities, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent

rules.detail: Once vested, hedging is treated as ordinary Trading requiring pre-approval; the Associated Product ban's wording is limited to the pre-vesting entitlement.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.

rules.detail: Monetisation (e.g. a prepaid forward) is not named; it would be 'agreeing to' sell Securities and so is Trading, with no pre-approval requirement for ordinary Genesis Energy Persons.
rules.evidence: 'Trading' in Securities means buying or selling securities, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent

rules.detail: Monetisation is not named; caught as Trading requiring pre-approval for Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.

rules.detail: Short selling is not named or separately addressed; selling (including a short sale) falls within 'Trading', so it is subject only to the insider trading and short-term trading rules for non-Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: 'Trading' in Securities means buying or selling securities, or agreeing to do so, whether as principal or agent

rules.detail: Short selling is not named; caught as Trading requiring pre-approval for Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.

rules.detail: Securities lending is not named anywhere in the Policy and lending is not a purchase, sale or agreement to trade, so it is not caught by the definition of Trading.
CFDs are not named but are a derivative product created in respect of Genesis Energy securities and so fall within Securities; no pre-approval requirement for non-Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: any options or derivatives (including futures contracts quoted on an authorised futures exchange) created over or in respect of any securities of any member of the Genesis Energy Group

rules.detail: CFDs are not named; caught as Trading requiring pre-approval for Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.

rules.detail: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending anywhere.
The Policy contains no reference to granting a charge, lien, pledge or other security over Genesis Energy Securities.
The Policy contains no reference to secured financing arrangements or a secured lender's enforcement rights, unlike most peer ASX policies.

Short-term Trading (buying and selling within a 3-month period) is discouraged and requires prior discussion with, and approval from, the General Counsel and Company Secretary, applying to all Genesis Energy Persons, not just Restricted Persons.
rules.evidence: You should not engage in short term Trading (i.e., the buying or selling within a 3 month period), unless there are exceptional circumstances, that are first discussed with and approved by the General Counsel and Company Secretary.

exemption_authority: Trading during a Blackout Period is prohibited except in exceptional circumstances (e.g. severe financial hardship or compulsion by court order/undertaking), approved by the Chairman of the Board (or, in the Chairman's absence, the Chairman of the Audit and Risk Committee) for Directors/Chief Executive requests, or by the Chief Executive in his/her sole discretion for other Restricted Persons; approval to trade in a Blackout Period is valid for only 2 trading days from notification and is deemed automatically withdrawn if the person becomes aware of Material Information before Trading.

bespoke_clauses.topic: Associated Product ban scoped to unvested entitlement
bespoke_clauses.clause: Where Genesis Energy Persons are entitled to participate in any equity-based remuneration scheme, they must not enter into any transaction for any 'Associated Product'. An Associated Product is any product which has the effect of limiting the economic risk of participating in any entitlement a Genesis Energy Person is eligible for under the remuneration scheme.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: This anti-hedging rule is framed around the unvested incentive entitlement, not shares already vested and held outright; on its literal wording a collar over vested, unrestricted shares is not caught, though this reading should be confirmed with the General Counsel and Company Secretary.

bespoke_clauses.clause: The Policy contains no reference to margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance, charges, pledges or a secured lender's enforcement rights.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: The loan leg of a funded collar is neither prohibited nor subject to any notification or disclosure duty under this Policy, unlike most ASX peer policies; that silence, and any separate NZ financial markets law overlay, should be checked before relying on it.

bespoke_clauses.topic: pre-approval required for every trade by Restricted Persons
bespoke_clauses.clause: Restricted Persons must seek pre-approval for any Trading in Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Every leg of a collar (entry, roll, unwind) by a director or senior manager needs prior written consent valid for only 10 trading days (2 trading days if granted during a Blackout Period), and lapses automatically if Material Information arises before execution.

bespoke_clauses.clause: You cannot avoid "Key Rule 1" by Trading in Securities through companies or trusts you control. If the companies or trusts that you control, Trade in Securities while you have Material Information, you will be deemed to have traded in the Securities.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Routing the collar or a related hedge through a controlled trust or company does not avoid the insider trading prohibition or the Restricted Person pre-approval requirement.

bespoke_clauses.clause: Securities means Ordinary shares of Genesis Energy which are quoted on the NZX Main Board and Australian Stock Exchange, Genesis Energy capital bonds quoted on the NZDX market, and NZ electricity futures contracts that are traded on ASX.
bespoke_clauses.why_it_matters: Both NZX and ASX disclosure regimes (and the Financial Markets Conduct Act 2013) can be triggered by a collar over Genesis Energy shares, in addition to this Policy's own approval and notification requirements.

summary: A funded collar over vested, unrestricted Genesis Energy shares appears achievable for Restricted Persons (directors, the Chief Executive and senior managers), subject to obtaining written pre-approval for the transaction -- from the Chief Executive, or the Chairman of the Board for Director/Chief Executive requests -- valid for 10 trading days (2 trading days if granted during a Blackout Period) and automatically withdrawn if Material Information comes to light. The Policy's only anti-hedging rule (the 'Associated Product' restriction) is framed around a person's unvested entitlement under an equity-based remuneration scheme, not securities already vested and held, so hedging of vested shares is not expressly banned on its wording, though this should be confirmed. Notably, the Policy contains no provision at all on margin lending, secured financing, encumbrance or a secured lender's enforcement rights, so the loan leg of the collar is neither prohibited nor subject to any notification duty under this document, though the silence and any NZ financial markets law overlay should be checked separately. Both the put/call derivatives and any monetisation fall within 'Securities'/'Trading' by definition (Securities expressly include options and derivatives), so they are subject to the same pre-approval and Blackout Period restrictions as an ordinary share trade, with post-trade details reported to the General Counsel and Company Secretary. The main residual constraints are the short-term trading discouragement (buying and selling within 3 months needs prior approval) and the Blackout Periods around each set of results and any prospectus, during which dealing needs exceptional-circumstances approval.
